items.description: Completed host turn → mininja_capture, or mininja_memory_commit if the user said remember. Key host-turn:<id>.
steps: Writer is the host runner on ~/mininja, not this console.
Default write is mininja_capture (raw_text, provenance = worktree + turn id).
Only if the user said remember / save this / add this as a fact: mininja_memory_commit.
Always pass idempotency_key = host-turn:<id>. Replay returns the original row.
Capture stays not immediately recallable. Do not promote.
items.regression_notes: Blocked until the host runner talks to the eleven MCP tools. Do not implement in this console. Do not use commitMemory, alice-continuity, or localStorage.

items.description: Terminal-failed host turn → one mininja_open_loops row. Same host-turn:<id>.
steps: On terminal failure, write one open loop. Label names the turn.
Put host-turn:<id> in the body or the id space already in use.
Do not also write a Mininja native task.
Do not use Track B openLoopCreate as the product write.
items.regression_notes: Blocked until the same host poller exists. A second task/board model is the thing the salvage retired.

items.description: Resolve the runner URL per call. Advance the high-water mark only after a fully clean batch.
steps: Resolve the runner / app URL on every call (port file or equivalent). Never cache it in a module const.
Seed the workspace/turn set on poller start. Do not wait for a live event.
Advance pollSince only after every item in the batch captured or looped cleanly.
A throw leaves the mark unmoved. Captures are idempotent, so re-fetch is safe.
Supervisor PATH must include the binaries the poller shells out to.
items.regression_notes: Blocked until the same host poller exists. These are the four 2026-07-05 defects that zeroed capture. Do not recur them.
